questions.question: According to Lowry-Brønsted, an acid is:
options: A substance that produces hydroxide ions in water

questions.question: A conjugate acid-base pair consists of two species that differ by exactly:
The conjugate base of hydrochloric acid is:
Water is called an ampholyte because it:
options: Can act as either a proton donor or a proton acceptor

subtopics.title: Strong, Weak, Concentrated, Dilute — and K a

questions.question: A STRONG acid is one that:
options: Has a low pH regardless of concentration

questions.question: The vinegar in your kitchen — plenty of ethanoic acid, barely ionised — is best described as:
A very small Ka value tells you the acid:
options: Ionises only partially — a weak acid

questions.question: Equal concentrations of a strong and a weak acid can be told apart because the strong acid:
options: Has a lower pH, conducts better, and reacts faster with magnesium
Is always more dangerous to touch

subtopics.title: pH, K w and the Calculations

questions.question: The pH of a 0,01 mol·dm⁻³ solution of hydrochloric acid is:
The pH of a 0,05 mol·dm⁻³ sulfuric acid solution (complete ionisation of both protons) is:
For 0,001 mol·dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide, using Kw = 1 × 10⁻¹⁴, the pH is:
Ethanoic acid at 0,01 mol·dm⁻³ has a pH noticeably HIGHER than 2 because:
options: Only a fraction of its molecules ionise, so the hydronium concentration is below 0,01
It contains fewer hydrogen atoms than HCl
Weak acids have no hydronium ions
The pH scale does not apply to weak acids

subtopics.title: Titrations, Indicators and the pH of Salts

questions.question: 25 cm³ of NaOH is exactly neutralised by 20 cm³ of 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ HCl. The NaOH concentration is:
The equivalence point of a titration is the moment when:
options: Acid and base have reacted in the exact mole ratio of the balanced equation

questions.question: A solution of ammonium chloride is slightly acidic because:
options: Chloride ions accept protons from water
The ammonium ion donates protons to water
The salt contains leftover hydrochloric acid

questions.question: For a titration of ethanoic acid with sodium hydroxide, the best indicator is:
options: Phenolphthalein, because the equivalence point lies above pH 7
Any indicator, since equivalence is always at 7

questions.question: In the pass-the-parcel picture, the parcel being handed over is:
When hydrochloric acid gives its proton to water, the products are:
options: The chloride ion and the hydronium ion
The chloride ion and the hydroxide ion
The hydronium ion and the hydroxide ion

questions.question: You can spot a conjugate pair by checking that the two species:
options: Differ by exactly one proton, with everything else the same
Appear on the same side of the equation

questions.question: In the cordial analogy, the amount of syrup poured into the glass stands for:
The syrup that splits up instantly and completely in water represents:
options: A strong acid — every molecule ionises
A weak acid — few molecules ionise

questions.question: "Pool-test drops" — a little acid, but all of it ionised — are an example of:
Ka is best described as:
options: The amount of acid in the bottle
The willingness to ionise, written as a number
The speed of the reaction with magnesium

subtopics.title: The Ladder of Tens and the Exact Balance

questions.question: A river's pH drops from 6 to 4. Its hydronium concentration has become:
Pure water sits at pH 7 because:
options: It contains no ions at all
It holds equal, tiny concentrations of hydronium and hydroxide
The scale was defined to start at 7

questions.question: A titration finds an unknown concentration by:
options: Matching the unknown exactly against a standard solution of known concentration
Reading the colour of the acid

questions.question: "The salt takes after its stronger parent" means, for the salt of a weak acid and a strong base, the equivalence solution is:
